description: Verify that DUT silently discards an IPv4 packet whose Destination Address is in the loopback range (127.0.0.0/8) when it arrives on a non-loopback interface — loopback traffic must never appear on the wire (RFC 1122 §3.2.1.3 'martian' filter)
approach:
[Objective]
The 127.0.0.0/8 prefix is reserved for the host's own loopback interface. A packet with a 127.x.x.x destination arriving via Ethernet is a 'martian' — either a misconfigured peer, a routing leak, or an attempt at spoofing. Hosts must drop it without response.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 packet on a non-loopback iface
   • dst_ip = 127.0.0.1 (or any 127.0.0.0/8 address)   ← key trigger

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: nothing — no reply, no error

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any response.

[Fail condition]
Fail_dut_replied — DUT responded despite the loopback dst_ip arriving on a non-loopback iface. Indicates the martian filter is missing.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the wire-arriving loopback packet — normal
verdicts.Fail_dut_replied: DUT responded to a wire-arriving 127.0.0.0/8 packet — martian filter missing
